front: What does the gradient of a distance–time graph give?
What does the gradient of a speed–time graph give?
What does the area under a speed–time graph give?
Horizontal line on a distance–time graph?
back: Stationary: the distance is not changing.

front: Horizontal line on a speed–time graph?

back: $\dfrac{\text{total distance}}{\text{total time}}$, including any stops (not the mean of the speeds).
Change in speed ÷ time taken, e.g. gaining $20\ \text{m/s}$ in $5\ \text{s}$ is $\frac{20}{5} = 4\ \text{m/s}^2$.

front: How do you convert km/h to m/s?
back: Multiply by $1000$ and divide by $3600$ (divide by $3.6$): $72\ \text{km/h} = 20\ \text{m/s}$.

front: Line sloping down to the time axis on a distance-from-home graph?
back: Travelling back home; the steepness gives the speed of return.

front: On a velocity–time graph, what does area below the time axis mean?
back: Movement in the opposite direction: it adds to the distance travelled but reduces the displacement.
